arxiv-1503-08048.title: Preferential imitation of vaccinating behavior can invalidate the targeted subsidy on complex networks
arxiv-1503-08048.creator: Hai-Feng Zhang, Pan-Pan Shu, Ming Tang, Michael Small
arxiv-1503-08048.description: Abstract We consider the effect of inducement to vaccinate during the spread of an infectious disease on complex networks. Suppose that public resources are finite and that only a small proportion of individuals can be vaccinated freely (complete subsidy), for the remainder of the population vaccination is a voluntary behavior — and each vaccinated individual carries a perceived cost.

arxiv-1905-12548.title: Digital Availability of Product Information for Collaborative Engineering of Spacecraft
arxiv-1905-12548.creator: Diana Peters, Philipp M. Fischer, Philipp M. Schäfer, Kobkaew Opasjumruskit, Andreas Gerndt
arxiv-1905-12548.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a system to collect product information from manufacturers and make it available in tools that are used for concurrent design of spacecraft. The planning of a spacecraft needs experts from different disciplines, like propulsion, power, and thermal.

arxiv-1909-06545.title: Topological inductive constructions for tight surface graphs Thanks: The second and third authors were supported by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council [grant number EP/P01108X/1]. Thanks: The fourth author gratefully acknowledges the financial support from the Iraqi Ministry of H
arxiv-1909-06545.creator: James Cruickshank, Derek Kitson, Stephen C. Power, Qays Shakir
arxiv-1909-06545.description: Abstract . We investigate properties of sparse and tight surface graphs. In particular we derive topological inductive constructions for ( 2 , 2 ) (2,2) -tight surface graphs in the case of the sphere, the plane, the twice punctured sphere and the torus.

arxiv-2012-08198.title: An analytical approach to symmetry breaking in multipole RF-traps
arxiv-2012-08198.creator: M. Marchenay, J. Pedregosa-Gutierrez, M. Knoop, M. Houssin, C. Champenois
arxiv-2012-08198.description: Abstract Radio-frequency linear multipole traps have been shown to be very sensitive to mis-positioning of their electrodes, which results in a symmetry breaking and leads to extra local minima in the trapping potential as shown in [ 1 ] disturbing the operation of the trap.

arxiv-2101-11580.title: Modeling of Nonlinear Interference Power for Dual-Polarization 4D Formats
arxiv-2101-11580.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . We assess the accuracy of a recently introduced nonlinear interference model for general dual-polarization 4D formats. Unlike previous models for polarization-multiplexed 2D formats, an average gap from split-step Fourier simulations within 0.1 dB is demonstrated.

arxiv-2105-13528.title: Improved finite-difference and pseudospectral schemes for the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with long-range temporal correlations Journal: Physica A
arxiv-2105-13528.creator: Xiongpeng Hu, Dapeng Hao, Hui Xia
arxiv-2105-13528.description: Abstract To investigate universal behavior and effects of long-range temporal correlations in kinetic roughening, we perform extensive simulations on the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation with temporally correlated noise based on pseudospectral (PS) and one of the improved finite-difference (FD) schemes. We find that scaling properties are affected by long-range temporal correlations within the effective temporally correlated regions.

arxiv-2112-05295.title: 3D Scene Understanding at Urban Intersection using Stereo Vision and Digital Map
arxiv-2112-05295.creator: Prarthana Bhattacharyya, Yanlei Gu, Jiali Bao, Xu Liu and Shunsuke Kamijo
arxiv-2112-05295.description: Abstract The driving behavior at urban intersections is very complex. It is thus crucial for autonomous vehicles to comprehensively understand challenging urban traffic scenes in order to navigate intersections and prevent accidents. In this paper, we introduce a stereo vision and 3D digital map based approach to spatially and temporally analyze the traffic situation at urban intersections.

arxiv-2206-11742.title: Inclusive and semi-inclusive production of spin-3/2 hadrons in e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} annihilation
arxiv-2206-11742.creator: Jing Zhao, Zhe Zhang, Zuo-tang Liang, Tianbo Liu, Ya-jin Zhou
arxiv-2206-11742.description: Abstract We investigate the inclusive and semi-inclusive productions of spin-3/2 hadrons, such as Ω \Omega , in unpolarized e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} annihilation. The general differential cross sections are expressed in terms of structure functions in accordance to the polarization of the hadron and the azimuthal modulations.

arxiv-2407-13439.title: Reducing Barriers to the Use of Marginalised Music Genres in AI Conference: Explainable AI for the Arts Workshop 2024; June 23, 2024; Chicago, IL, United States
arxiv-2407-13439.creator: Nick Bryan-Kinns, Zijin Li
arxiv-2407-13439.description: Abstract . AI systems for high quality music generation typically rely on extremely large musical datasets to train the AI models. This creates barriers to generating music beyond the genres represented in dominant datasets such as Western Classical music or pop music.

arxiv-2409-14443.title: Cosmological eras with the neutrino non-relativistic transition in RTB gravity
arxiv-2409-14443.creator: Jonas Pinheiro da Silva, Hermano Velten
arxiv-2409-14443.description: Abstract Theories based on the Ricci and the trace of the energy-momentum tensor, or the short name Ricci-trace-based (RTB) theories, represent a gravitational approach based on the Ricci scalar R R , and the trace of the energy-momentum tensor g μ ​ ν ​ T μ ​ ν = T g^{\mu\nu}T_{\mu\nu}=T .

arxiv-2501-12022.title: Foreign Object Segmentation in Chest X-Rays through Anatomy-guided Shape Insertion
arxiv-2501-12022.creator: Constantin Seibold, Hamza Kalisch, Lukas Heine, Simon Reiß, Jens Kleesiek
arxiv-2501-12022.description: Abstract In this paper, we tackle the challenge of instance segmentation for foreign objects in chest radiographs, commonly seen in postoperative follow-ups with stents, pacemakers, or ingested objects in children. The diversity of foreign objects complicates dense annotation, as shown in insufficient existing datasets.

arxiv-2601-03683.title: Rethinking Recurrent Neural Networks for Time Series Forecasting: A Reinforced Recurrent Encoder with Prediction-Oriented Proximal Policy Optimization Journal: journal
arxiv-2601-03683.creator: Xin Lai, Shiming Deng, Lu Yu, Yumin Lai, Shenghao Qiao, Xinze Zhang
arxiv-2601-03683.description: Abstract Time series forecasting plays a crucial role in contemporary engineering information systems for supporting decision-making across various industries, where Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) have been widely adopted due to their capability in modeling sequential data. Conventional RNN-based predictors adopt an encoder-only strategy with sliding historical windows as inputs to forecast future values.

pmc-11300829.title: Mechanism of arsenic removal using brown seaweed derived impregnated with iron oxide biochar for batch and column studies
pmc-11300829.creator: Satesh Kumar Devrajani, Zubair Ahmed, Naveed Ahmed Qambrani, Sania Kanwal, Uma Maheswari Sundaram, Nabisab Mujawar Mubarak
pmc-11300829.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Water contaminated with arsenic presents serious health risks, necessitating effective and sustainable removal methods. This article proposes a method for removing arsenic from water by impregnating biochar with iron oxide (Fe2O3) from brown seaweed (Sargassum polycystum). After the seaweed biomass was pyrolyzed at 400 °C, iron oxide was added to the biochar to increase its adsorptive sites and surface functional groups, which allowed the binding of arsenic ions.

pmc-11403645.title: Evaluation of CTLA-4 and PD-L1 Expression in Thyroid Carcinoma and Its Prognostic Significance
pmc-11403645.creator: Nidhi Anand, Pallavi Srivastava, Nuzhat Husain, Deeksha Agarwal, Anurag Gupta, Roma Pradhan
pmc-11403645.description: IntroductionImmune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) have revolutionised treatment and improved outcomes in various malignancies. We aimed to evaluate CTLA-4 and PD-L1 immunoexpression in thyroid tumours and correlated them with clinicopathological parameters.MethodsThe study included 90 cases of thyroid malignancies comprising papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) (n = 64, 54.

pmc-11429379.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMetabolic syndrome (MetS) in older adults with hypertension, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia increases the risks of cardiovascular diseases by 2.5 times and type 2 diabetes by five times. pmc-11712743.title: Impact of TDP‐43 co‐pathology on limbic cortical microstructure in Alzheimer's disease: evidence from an autopsy‐confirmed cohort with in vivo diffusion MRI
pmc-11712743.creator: Mario Torso, Gerard R Ridgway, Jamie Hardwidge, Ian Hardingham, Steven A Chance, National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI)
pmc-11712743.description: BackgroundTDP‐43 (TAR DNA‐binding protein 43) is one of the most frequently observed co‐pathologies in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Recognizing the diversity of pathological features in individuals with AD, including the presence of TDP‐43, may lead to more personalized and effective treatment approaches.

pmc-11862675.title: Sexuality in patients treated for borderline personality disorder at the Arrazi psychiatric hospital in Salé
pmc-11862675.creator: N. Ait Bensaid, Y. Bensalah, M. Sabir, F. El Omari
pmc-11862675.description: IntroductionBorderline personality disorder is a severe mental disorder characterized by generalized instability of emotional regulation of interpersonal relationships and self-image, and marked impulsivity. Several features of this disorder are likely to be associated with problematic sexual health, such as impulsivity (impulsive sexual behavior), identity disorders (unstable sexual identity) and unstable and intense interpersonal relationships.

pmc-12454509.title: Effects of Displacement Piles for Dike Reinforcement on Adjacent Buildings
pmc-12454509.creator: Majd Ahmad, Ronald B J Brinkgreve, Sebastiaan N Jonkman
pmc-12454509.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation into the use of displacement piles as a reinforcement measure for river dikes founded on soft soil, with a particular focus on geotechnical performance, macro stability, and impacts on nearby buildings. A finite element model is developed using parameters derived from a representative Dutch dike case (Bergambacht), incorporating the Hardening Soil, Soft Soil Creep and NGI-ADP-SHANSEP models to capture soil behaviour.

pmc-13126436.title: Rate of Hearing Loss in Platinum‐Naïve Patients Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors
pmc-13126436.creator: Kaitlyn A. Brooks, Christopher G. Gidley, Olivia Grimley, Catherine Wang, Shirin Jivani, Dianna Roberts, Aung Naing, Jack Phan, Katherine Hutcheson, Xin Wang, Paul W. Gidley, Marc‐Elie Nader
pmc-13126436.description: ObjectiveHearing loss from immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has been documented in case reports and case series. We present the largest retrospective study investigating the rate of ICI‐related ototoxicity in a monitored cohort of platinum‐naïve patients.Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingTertiary‐care center.MethodsPatients treated with ICI between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2022, with baseline and post‐treatment audiograms, were included.

pmc-13182423.title: Impact of long COVID on diverse Australian populations: a multi-site, longitudinal prospective cohort study protocol
pmc-13182423.creator: Shiqi Luo, Zhen Zheng, Leila Karimi, Magdalena Plebanski, Kate Louise McCann Anderson, Natalie Jovanovski, Chintha Lankatillake, Wendell Cockshaw, Dennis Wollersheim, Jacob Sheahan, Emma-Louise Seal, Kerryn Butler-Henderson, Donald Campbell, April Clarke, Sonja Cleary, Jessica Danaher, Doa El-Ansary
pmc-13182423.description: BackgroundLong COVID is a complex, multisystem chronic condition that may persist or fluctuate for months to years after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Despite emerging international research, significant gaps remain in understanding the full breadth of long COVID’s impacts in Australia. No study has yet prospectively examined these multidimensional impacts using a culturally appropriate, user-validated toolkit.
